summary: Uruguay’s pledges mix conservation, restoration and agriculture. By 2030, it seeks to protect all 849,960 ha of native forest recorded in 2012 and optionally add 5% (42,498 ha); the latter equals about 1.8% of its currently mapped forest, while reversing degradation across 892,460 ha. Conservation goals include protecting 50% of 2020 peatlands, covering every vulnerable coastal component in adaptation plans, preparing six watershed plans, and reducing natural-grassland loss by 50% in 2026–2030. Agricultural actions extend good natural-field management over 1.5–4.0 million ha—12.5–33.4% of current grassland—and target 95% of agricultural area under soil-management plans, plus rice irrigation, dairy, fertilizer and soil-carbon measures. By 2035, Uruguay targets climate-risk plans in all protected areas, 10 watershed/aquifer plans, heat-stress measures on 70% of holdings, while newer forest pledges seek 20% expansions in managed plantations and shelter areas.
